title: How do we continue a pattern of tenth numbers?
description: Six patterns of numbers with tenths each have a steady change, found by taking one number from the next. The change is added or taken away four more times. Keeko doubts the first change and reads three tenths as three.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the change between two neighbouring numbers and use it again and again. Watch for students who read the change as the digit written in the tenths and drop the word tenths.

video_script.why: The child can add and subtract numbers with tenths and now uses the difference of two neighbours to continue six patterns.
video_script.substitution: Take the earlier number from the later one to find the change, then add or take away that change four more times.
video_script.anchor: Six number patterns written in rows, each with two or three numbers shown and four empty boxes after them
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the change in the first pattern as the digit 3 and adds 3 instead of 3 tenths, but 4 to 4 3/10 grows by only 3 tenths.
video_script.payoff_line: The first pattern goes on to four and nine tenths, then five and two tenths

final_answer.spoken: the first pattern goes on to four and nine tenths, five and two tenths, five and five tenths, and five and eight tenths

maths_rules: Pattern 4: 5 3/10 is 4/10 less than 5 7/10, take away 4/10 each time: 4 9/10, 4 5/10, 4 1/10, 3 7/10.
Pattern 5: 13 is 5/10 less than 13 5/10, take away 5/10 each time: 12, 11 5/10, 11, 10 5/10.
Pattern 6: 10 4/10 is 1 1/10 less than 11 5/10, take away 1 1/10 each time: 8 2/10, 7 1/10, 6, 4 9/10.
Slip: the change 3/10 is read as 3.
video_script.design: One idea: the change between two neighbours is used again and again. Assumes the child can add and subtract numbers with tenths. Wrong idea: read the tenths digit as a whole number. The six rows stay all video; the working band shows the changes and the answer beat fills the boxes. Most of the numbers are on the board and not spoken.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='seq'/>Look at the numbers four, four and three tenths, and four and six tenths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>They follow a pattern. What are the next four numbers?

beats.on_screen: the pattern stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: three numbers on a number line with an equal jump drawn between each neighbouring pair; the jump is labelled the change

marks.same: equal jumps appear between the neighbouring numbers on a number line
marks.sub: the jump is labelled the change = later number - earlier number
marks.down: a jump going left is shown beside the jump going right

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>In a pattern, each number comes from the one before by the same change.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>To find the change, take the earlier number from the later number.
<bookmark mark='down'/>If the numbers go down, we take the change away each time.

marks.given: the six patterns are written in six rows, each with four empty boxes after it

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six patterns. Each one has its first two or three numbers written on the board.

beats.on_screen: To find: the change in each pattern, and the next four numbers

marks.find: the words the change and the next four numbers are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the change in each pattern, and then the next four numbers.

marks.one: the first two patterns go up and are marked with an up arrow

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, the first two patterns go up.
<bookmark mark='p1'/>Four and three tenths take away four leaves three tenths, so we add three tenths each time.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>Eight and seven tenths take away eight and two tenths leaves five tenths. We add five tenths each time.

<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, the third pattern also goes up. Eight and seven tenths take away seven and six tenths leaves one and one tenth. <bookmark mark='p3'/>We add one and one tenth each time.

beats.on_screen: Pattern 4: 5 3/10 is 4/10 less than 5 7/10, take away 4/10; Pattern 5: 13 is 5/10 less than 13 5/10, take away 5/10; Pattern 6: 10 4/10 is 1 1/10 less than 11 5/10, take away 1 1/10

marks.three: the last three patterns go down and are marked with a down arrow
marks.p4: Pattern 4 shows 5 3/10 is 4/10 less than 5 7/10, take away 4/10
marks.p5: Pattern 5 shows 13 is 5/10 less than 13 5/10, take away 5/10
marks.p6: Pattern 6 shows 10 4/10 is 1 1/10 less than 11 5/10, take away 1 1/10

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, the last three patterns go down.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>Five and three tenths is four tenths less than five and seven tenths. We take away four tenths each time.
<bookmark mark='p5'/>Thirteen is five tenths less than thirteen and five tenths. We take away five tenths each time.
<bookmark mark='p6'/>Ten and four tenths is one and one tenth less than eleven and five tenths. We take away one and one tenth each time.

beats.on_screen: add or take away the change four times in each pattern

marks.four: an arrow loops four times over the boxes of each pattern
marks.new: each new box is joined by an arrow to the box before it

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, use the change again and again. We add or take away the change four times in every pattern. <bookmark mark='new'/>Each new number comes from the one before it.

marks.ans: the four boxes of the first pattern fill in one after another
marks.rest: the boxes of the other five patterns fill in and the answer is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The first pattern goes on to four and nine tenths, then five and two tenths.
It reaches five and five tenths, and five and eight tenths.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The other five patterns are written on the board, found the same way.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 4 to 4 3/10: add 3 each time; the number line shows the jump from 4 to 4 3/10 as a small jump inside one unit; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.doubt: the bubble add 3 each time appears
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the small jump from 4 to 4 3/10 glows inside one unit

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we add three each time, because the number three is written in the first pattern.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But that three counts tenths, so the jump is only three tenths. The numbers grow by a small part, not by three whole units.
